chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

Whichever of the two matters precedes her, her waiting period is fulfilled: if three months pass and she does not see blood in them, her waiting period is fulfilled; and if three pure periods pass, her waiting period is fulfilled.

key_terms.أَحَدِهِمَا: One of the two (referring to the 5th or 6th Imam)

ai.seo_question: How is the waiting period calculated for a woman with irregular menstruation according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the dual criteria for the waiting period (iddah) of a mustahaddah (woman with irregular menstruation), prioritizing whichever condition—three months of amenorrhea or three menstrual cycles—is met first. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling resolves the ambiguity of irregular bleeding by providing a clear, time-based alternative to standard menstrual counting, ensuring legal certainty for remarriage. The emphasis on 'whichever comes first' reflects the juristic principle of taking the easier path for the woman while maintaining the sanctity of lineage and marital boundaries.
